messages.text: Good news on that one — the WS2000 is a weather station, not a miner, so power is a rounding error on your bill, not a cost to plan around. It earns WXM for reporting real weather from your spot. Do you have somewhere open to mount it, like a roof or pole?
Searched the catalog · WeatherXM WS2000 weather station

Then you're set. The WS2000 is $400, runs on AA batteries for about 1.5 years, no wiring and no WiFi — it reports over the Helium network, and you earn WXM for the data. Setup is about 30 minutes.

Want me to build the cart?
can i see how many other xm stations are in my area

Yes — WeatherXM has a public map at explore.weatherxm.com. Zoom to your address and you'll see every live station and the gaps around you. Density matters: fewer stations nearby generally means better rewards for yours.

Tell me your town and I'll take a look with you.

I can't pull the live map into the chat, so that one's a 10-second job on your end: explore.weatherxm.com, search (postcode hidden), and count the pins within a few miles.

South Hills is suburban and the network is thin outside the big metros, so odds are you'd be filling a gap. Want the cart ready either way?
